newsitem.title: USA: Hillsborough Cty, Fla., seeks Bucs bond validation.
newsitem.headline: Hillsborough Cty, Fla., seeks Bucs bond validation.

text.p: Florida's Hillsborough County Commission voted unanimously to seek court validation for the legally disputed bonds it plans to issue for the Tampa Bay Bucanneers' new stadium, county officials said Wednesday.
That could clear the way for the bonds to be sold by the end of April, County Attorney Emeline Acton said.
Tampa Sports Authority agreed to sell $168 million of revenue bonds for the stadium, backed with revenues from a sales tax increase approved by voters in September.
Former Mayor William Poe sued to block the plan, claiming it would unconstitutionally use public money for a project that would mainly benefit the private, for-profit football team.
A Hillsborough County judge dismissed the suit and Poe appealed to the 2nd District Court of Appeal in Lakeland.
The appeals court scheduled a hearing on Jan 14, but a decision may not come for several months afterward and the case could still be appealed to the state Supreme Court.
If the bonds are validated the county could proceed with the issue.
County commissioners approved a validation request Tuesday night, and the sports authority has also agreed. The Tampa City Commission is expected to give approval Thursday.

The project is up against two deadlines for the stadium -- a contract calling for the arena to be finished in time for the 1998 football season, and the threat of a bill by U.S. Sen. Patrick Moynihan, D-N.Y., which would end tax-exempt bond financing for professional sports facilities.
